verdict.reason: Ikuhara's surreal anime masterpiece transforms Revolutionary Girl Utena into pure cinema. The film's visual complexity rewards the big screen treatment it rarely receives.

ratings.plot: Autumn Moon (Sam Lee), a low-rent triad living in Hong Kong, struggles to find meaning in his hopelessly violent existence.

verdict.reason: One of the essential films of Hong Kong's handover period that deserves a big screen viewing. Chan shoots with handheld 16mm that captures the raw energy of street-level desperation better than any digital transfer.

ratings.plot: In Paris outskirts Blanche, a young clerk, befriends Lea, a girl livelier than she is. Lea is going steady with Fabien who is a friend to Alexandre who is going steady with Adrienne but is however loved by Blanche. Somehow a way h...

verdict.reason: Peak Rohmer that captures the entire Moral Tales project in microcosm. The dialogue rhythms and behavioral precision reward theatrical attention.

ratings.plot: Eight-year-old Ahmed has mistakenly taken his friend Mohammad's notebook. He wants to return it, or else his friend will be expelled from school. The boy determinedly sets out to find Mohammad's home in the neighbouring village.

verdict.reason: Kiarostami's breakthrough transforms a simple premise into profound cinema. The Iranian landscape and natural light create images that lose impact on small screens.

ratings.plot: Pulp novelist Holly Martins travels to shadowy, postwar Vienna, only to find himself investigating the mysterious death of an old friend, Harry Lime.

verdict.reason: Essential viewing on the big screen where Reed's tilted camera angles and deep focus photography can work their full magic. The zither music and Vienna's bombed-out sewers create an atmosphere that streaming cannot match.

ratings.plot: Paddington, now happily settled with the Brown family and a popular member of the local community, picks up a series of odd jobs to buy the perfect present for his Aunt Lucy's 100th birthday, only for the gift to be stolen.

verdict.reason: This is as close to perfect family filmmaking as you can get. Paul King turns every frame into a handcrafted dollhouse where even the prison sequence feels like a warm hug.

movies.title: Marcel the Shell with Shoes On

ratings.plot: A cash-strapped documentary maker decides to make his newest documentary about a mollusk shell he finds living in his Airbnb with his friends.

verdict.reason: This deserves the biggest screen you can find for a film that transforms intimate stop-motion into genuine magic. Fleischer Camp's direction makes Marcel's tiny world feel vast and emotionally enormous.

ratings.plot: Joe and Angela's marriage is on thin ice. When they invite their enigmatic upstairs neighbors for a dinner party, the night spirals into unexpected places.

verdict.reason: Wilde has made a sharp film about the theater of modern marriage that earns its runtime. The dinner party structure creates genuine tension without relying on cheap thriller mechanics.

ratings.plot: They talk about the beautiful game, but for Laurentiu Ginghina, it's not enough. Football must be modified, streamlined, freed from restraints; corners are to be rounded off, players assigned to zones and subteams, norms revised. ...

verdict.reason: Worth the trip for one of cinema's most quietly absurd philosophical comedies. Porumboiu turns a man's obsession with redesigning football into a deadpan masterpiece about Romanian bureaucratic thinking.

ratings.plot: A frigid young housewife decides to spend her midweek afternoons as a prostitute.

verdict.reason: Essential Buñuel that demands the big screen for its dreamlike visual transitions and precise framing. Catherine Deneuve gives one of cinema's great performances about the mysteries of desire.

ratings.plot: Mysterious boat returns to a village 30 years after vanishing. Two men join its crew hoping for better fortune. After one voyage, they find themselves transported back in time, mistaken for the original crew.

verdict.reason: Mark Jenkin has made another essential folk horror that demands the big screen. His handmade 16mm photography creates textures that streaming will flatten into nothing.

ratings.plot: In 2075, a girl witnesses a mysterious boy in a rainbow suit fall from the sky. He comes from an idyllic far future where time travel is possible. She shelters him and will do whatever it takes to help him return to his time.

verdict.reason: This animated time-travel story delivers visual invention that justifies the theatrical experience. Director Ugo Bienvenu crafts a rainbow-suited aesthetic that demands the biggest screen you can find.

ratings.plot: Two neighbors form a strong bond after both suspect extramarital activities of their spouses. However, they agree to keep their bond platonic so as not to commit similar wrongs.

verdict.reason: Worth the trip for Wong Kar-wai's most complete achievement. Christopher Doyle's cinematography creates a world of longing that demands the big screen.

ratings.plot: Two teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most - each other.

verdict.reason: Chiarella crafts a genuinely fresh take on body horror that earns its high concept through committed performances. The 88-minute runtime keeps the tension tight without overstaying its welcome.

ratings.plot: Showgirls Lorelei Lee and Dorothy Shaw travel to Paris, pursued by a private detective hired by the suspicious father of Lorelei's fiancé, as well as a rich, enamored old man and many other doting admirers.

verdict.reason: Essential Hawks on a big screen where Monroe and Russell's chemistry can work its full magic. The Technicolor musical numbers demand theatrical presentation to capture their lavish spectacle.

ratings.plot: Follows the Jackass crew as they perform their final series of dangerous stunts and pranks, marking the end of the franchise.

verdict.reason: This is the farewell tour for a comedy franchise that demands to be experienced with a crowd. The mix of new stunts and greatest hits creates the rare compilation that works as both nostalgia trip and fresh entertainment.

ratings.plot: The ethereally beautiful Vicky recalls her romances with Hao Hao and Jack in the neon-lit clubs of Taipei.

verdict.reason: Essential Hou Hsiao-hsien that turns club culture into pure cinema poetry. The neon-soaked visuals and Shu Qi's magnetic performance demand the biggest screen you can find.

ratings.plot: During Prohibition, Treasury agent Eliot Ness sets out to stop ruthless Chicago gangster Al Capone, and assembles a small, incorruptible team to help him.

verdict.reason: Worth seeing on the big screen for De Palma's operatic take on the gangster genre. The Odessa Steps homage alone justifies the theatrical experience.

ratings.plot: During the Vietnam War, a soldier finds himself the outsider of his own squad when they unnecessarily kidnap a female villager, for their sexual enjoyment.

verdict.reason: Essential De Palma that demands the big screen for its brutal moral clarity. The director's trademark split-screen techniques turn the Vietnam horror into a cinematic trial by fire.

ratings.plot: If you found out we weren't alone, if someone showed you, proved it to you, would that frighten you?

verdict.reason: Spielberg tackling alien contact is worth the trip for any serious moviegoer. The director's mastery of wonder and dread makes this the rare sci-fi thriller that demands the big screen experience.

ratings.plot: Cat is a solitary animal, but as its home is devastated by a great flood, he finds refuge on a boat populated by various species, and will have to team up with them despite their differences.

verdict.reason: Rare wordless storytelling that succeeds entirely through visual language and deserves the largest screen possible. Zilbalodis crafts each frame with painterly precision that streaming compression would diminish.

ratings.plot: After breaking the mysterious "One Wish Willow" to win his crush's heart, a hopeless romantic finds himself getting exactly what he asked for but soon discovers that some desires come at a dark, sinister price.

verdict.reason: Generic horror premise dressed up with high production values that cannot mask thin storytelling. Barker's direction lacks the innovation needed to elevate familiar wish-fulfillment scares.

ratings.plot: Follows the Minions in 1920s Hollywood as they search for frightening creatures for their monster movie, partner with a green creature, and must save the planet after unleashing monsters.

verdict.reason: Skip it unless you have kids who demand the theatrical experience. Pierre Coffin's direction has grown stale over five films, relying on the same physical gags that worked better in the original Despicable Me.

ratings.plot: The early life of musician Michael Jackson, from the discovery of his talent as the lead of the Jackson Five to the artist whose creative ambition fueled a pursuit to become the biggest entertainer in the world.

verdict.reason: Skip this sanitized biopic that treats Jackson like a product to be marketed. Fuqua's direction lacks the complexity needed to handle such a controversial figure.

ratings.plot: Kara Zor-El, aka Supergirl, joins forces with an unlikely companion on an interstellar journey of vengeance and justice when an unexpected adversary strikes too close to home.

verdict.reason: Save your money for a better superhero film this year. Gillespie's direction feels completely wrong for cosmic-scale action, turning what should be epic into something awkwardly small.

Before the factories emptied out and the Motor City lost its shine, Detroit was all horsepower, soul, and swagger. MOTOR CITY drops you into that world, following a working-class romantic who gets framed by a ruthless gangster after falling for the wrong woman. Years later, he's out of prison with one thing on his mind: revenge. Starring Alan Ritchson and Shailene Woodley, MOTOR CITY is a stylish throwback crime thriller fueled by muscle cars, sharp suits, and a killer soundtrack curated by Jack White. If you like your revenge stories lean, mean, and set to impeccable needle drops, this one's built to go fast.

Winner of over 35 awards, experience the best of British musical HER-story in a live capture of the must-see musical sensation, SIX the Musical . The original West End cast reunite at London’s Vaudeville Theatre in front of a sold-out audience to strut their stuff and rewrite their Tudor traumas in an unmissable cinematic recording of the show packed full of style, sass, and sensational songs. Watched by audiences of over 3.5 million, SIX the Musical has become a global theatre phenomenon since its 2017 debut at Edinburgh Festival Fringe, where it has redefined the boundaries of musical theatre. The show tells the extraordinary story of the six wives of King Henry VIII, who step out of the shadow of their infamous husband and reclaim their own narratives.

verdict.reason: Worth it if you love the show enough to sing along in public, but the theatrical energy gets lost in translation to cinema. The original West End cast delivers the vocals with precision, but filmed musicals rarely capture what makes live theater electric.

Mob is an 8th grader with powerful psychic abilities who wants to be normal. When not exorcising evil spirits, he attempts to suppress his powers, causing stunted emotions. But when he hits 100 percent, his pent-up feelings unleash a dark power. Can he survive the psychic strain?

Don’t think ELF is one of the best holiday films ever? You sit on a throne of lies! Christmas movies come and go, but few join the pantheon of the greats. You know the ones – A CHRISTMAS STORY, IT'S A WONDERFUL LIFE, and MIRACLE ON 34TH STREET. These are just a few that are invited to sit at the adult table of holiday movies. While the last couple of decades have been pretty sparse when it comes to quality Christmas movies, ELF, the 2003 Will Ferrell comedy, undoubtedly has taken a corner seat at this proverbial table of fame. Directed by Jon Favreau, ELF is one of those Christmas movies that's impossible to not love It's funny in all the right places, highly quotable, and surprisingly tender. It's Will Ferrell at his Ferrellist. Don't miss a full night of pointy-toed, jingle bell bliss – especially if you need a pick-me-up in the holiday cheer department – because attending ELF is the Christmas spirit equivalent of putting syrup on your spaghetti.

ratings.plot: High stakes. Blazing speed. Heart-pounding action. A brotherhood fueled by adrenaline. Welcome to the world of underground street racing. At the turn of the millennium, audiences across the world were introduced to a pulse-pounding, pedal-to-the-metal saga that would forever redefine the action genre... but it started on the streets. Enter THE FAST AND THE FURIOUS, a high-octane thriller that follows undercover cop Brian O'Conner (Paul Walker) as he infiltrates the world of illegal street racing led by charismatic criminal Dominic Toretto (Vin Diesel). As loyalties are tested and relationships forged, an unforgettable partnership is born between the two rivals. Combining the relentless speed of high-performance cars with jaw-dropping action sequences, THE FAST AND THE FURIOUS introduced a new breed of action heroes and sparked a legendary franchise. Witness the birth of a phenomenon that changed the way we experience action movies and ignited our desire for more.

“The most sickly entertaining theatrical experience of the year.” – IndieWire Oh, the things we do for beauty. Look, we’re not saying we wouldn’t want to look like Margaret Qualley, but Demi Moore’s over-the-hill aerobic star goes to some pretty extreme measures. Her use of THE SUBSTANCE may transform her into a “younger, more beautiful, more perfect” version of herself (via a gloriously horrific rebirth), but the more she uses it, the worse the side effects become. It becomes increasingly apparent that beauty is only skin deep as both of her lives spiral into a truly ugly mess. THE SUBSTANCE is a wild, toe-curling ride from writer/director Coralie Fargeat that features some of the most nerve-shredding body horror sequences in recent years. And with it taking home the award for Best Screenplay at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival, there’s plenty of substance behind the camera as well. As fantastical as the beauty solution is, THE SUBSTANCE’s themes of aging, youth, and self-esteem are very much grounded in our obsession with physical beauty.

40 YEARS OF FUCKIN' UP is SPINAL TAP, but real. It's a film about the infamous, fairly unfamous, and beloved punk rock band NOFX. This is the unbelievable story about how a group of untalented, drug-addicted teenage punks somehow became the most successful independent band in history – and they did it haphazardly, entirely on their own.

In this charming little parlor, you don't just get your hair and nails did – you get life lessons from some of the best and sassiest actresses to ever grace the screen. Without STEEL MAGNOLIAS, how would you know that there are so many different shades of pink (including Blush and Bashful), or that all gay men have track lighting? Without Ouiser Boudreaux (Shirley MacLaine, in all of her cantankerously awesome glory), how would you discover that it's possible to be in a bad mood for 40 years? And without Clairee Belcher (Olympia Dukakis), how would you learn that the only thing that separates us from animals is our ability to accessorize? Don't even get us started on Truvy Jones (Dolly Parton), whose folksy wisdom and bedazzled ensembles basically make life worth living. These ladies are guaranteed to inspire you just as sure as they'll make you bawl your eyes out and then crack you up, because we all know laughter through tears is the best emotion. So tease up your hair, grab your bestie, and join us for a cinematic celebration of friendship, perms, and Southern living. It'll be even better than a slice of armadillo cake.

Remember those kids who were too cool for school? Those kids are now your camp counselors. David Wain and company (including members of MTV's The State , the Upright Citizens Brigade, SNL , and a pre-famed Bradley Cooper) make idiosyncratic, over-the-top. strangely touching comedy. These character creations are unlike anything you've ever seen AND people you can relate to. There's young love, steamy sessions in the shed, talking cans, and everybody's favorite activity...going to town! So relive this unbelievably watchable, funny, original movie. It doesn't give one single f*ck...and that's the best part.

ratings.plot: It's a BRAND NEW DAY for Peter Parker. Fighting crime full-time as Spider-Man in a world that doesn’t remember him – and the pressure of seeing his old friends move on without him – sparks a change in Peter he may not have the power to control. But that transformation might also be the only thing that can stop a shocking new threat to the city and those he loves – a powerful villain no one can even see. It’s always a big day when your friendly neighborhood Spider-Man swings into Alamo Drafthouse – and we’re going all in for this one: An exclusive SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY menu of drinks and shakes, available at all shows 7/28-8/17. The highest presentation standards in the biz – see it in stunning HDR or on our massive Big Show screens. Our signature ad-free preshow with vintage Spidey clips and other rarities we’ve picked out just for BRAND NEW DAY. The world may have forgotten Peter Parker, but we haven't.

How do you follow up a heavy-hitting, multiple Oscar-winning blockbuster like OPPENHEIMER? If you're Christopher Nolan, you tackle one of the most influential stories ever told. THE ODYSSEY brings Homer's ancient Greek epic to the big screen with Matt Damon as Odysseus, a warrior king trying to get home after the Trojan War. What should be a straightforward trip turns into a decade-long odyssey filled with peril, adventure, and one setback after another. Basically, it's an epic story about an all-time terrible commute. Make no doubt about it, this is a movie built for the big screen, and Alamo Drafthouse is the place to experience it.

Two-time GRAMMY®-nominated global girl group KATSEYE is coming to cinemas worldwide with a special theatrical release ahead of their third EP, WILD . KATSEYE: WILD HEARTS is a captivating journey into the group's bold new era while celebrating the fans who helped make it possible. Featuring never-before-seen footage, EYEKONS fan videos, and intimate interviews from the group members, the film explores the powerful bond between KATSEYE and their global fandom. A love letter to the EYEKONS who helped build this movement, KATSEYE: WILD HEARTS reveals why this group's story is only just beginning. From the intense pressure of Dream Academy to chart-topping viral success, audiences experience the highs, setbacks, sacrifices, and breakthrough moments that transformed KATSEYE on their path to global pop stardom. Praised by outlets including The New York Times , Vogue , Rolling Stone , and Billboard , KATSEYE has earned acclaim for their relentless dedication to their craft and electrifying live performances. As one of pop's most exciting emerging global acts, the group continues to solidify its place as a worldwide force. From the same team that created Netflix’s POP STAR ACADEMY, KATSEYE: WILD HEARTS is produced by Interscope Films and Boardwalk Pictures, in partnership with HYBE X GEFFEN, and directed by Nadia Hallgren.

One voice. One unforgettable spectacle. SIA: NOSTALGIC FOR THE PRESENT is a bold, genre-defying experience that trades pop pageantry for pure artistry. Awe-inspiring vocals, breathtaking choreography, and iconic performances, captured cinematically and soundtracked by an unmatched catalog of hits. In 2016, Sia toured the world, mirroring this film live on stage, frame for frame. Remastered for its tenth anniversary, it stands alone for the first time – not as a concert film, but as a visual masterpiece unlike anything in music since. Starring Maddie Ziegler, Kristen Wiig, Paul Dano, Ben Mendelsohn, Gaby Hoffmann, and Tig Notaro. Choreographed by Ryan Heffington. Directed by Sia and Daniel Askill.

A direct continuation of the first three films in the SAW voyage, SAW IV mutates the format to share the origin story of mysterious serial killer Jigsaw, his traps, and Billy, his faithful puppet. This grimy, unforgiving squirm-machine exchanges the Michael Bay-style action of the previous two entries for an overdose of soap opera histrionics. Plus some of the most vomitously beautiful practical gore effects of the Y2K era. SAW IV is another reminder that this franchise was built to be experienced big, loud, and in a theater full of appreciative gorehounds. To quote Jigsaw: “It’s not over, the games have just begun.”

Imagine that a local cable station was invaded by otherdimensional creatures at the stroke of midnight. That's Video Vortex. Each month, this series presents a mystery transmission that's culled from the outer limits of home video history – from essential underground films to surreal docs, from tokusatsu battle-parties to outsider experiments. So warm up the cathode tubes, dim the lights, and let your senses intermingle with the glow.

verdict.reason: Worth it if you enjoy digging through VHS obscurities with an audience that gets the joke. The curation is solid but the format means you never know if you'll get gold or cheese.

When 13 GOING ON 30 was released over 20 years ago(!), I was overjoyed at the fact that Hollywood had finally decided to make BIG for girls. Don't get me wrong, it was awesome to watch Tom Hanks spend his paycheck on video games and a penthouse with a trampoline, but now it was a gal's turn to live the dream, and Jennifer Garner did not disappoint. This film features the greatest fantasies of a 13-year-old girl*: a makeover montage in a gigantic closet, a high-power job working at a fashion magazine, a massive slumber party, and, of course, a totally cute guy. But 13 GOING ON 30 isn't just a fun premise, it's a heartfelt and hilarious coming-of-age story. The cast is top-notch, with Garner perfectly embodying her inner teen, Judy Greer serving up some major sass (like she does), and Mark Ruffalo being as foxy and charming as he's ever been. This delightful cinematic concoction is better than a pack of Razzles, so join us and experience the thrill of being 30, flirty, and thriving. *Or any girl, regardless of her age. Because that shoe collection! WANT. (Sarah Pitre)
